questions: If multiple good sequences exist for the same A, are we summing their scores as integers before taking modulo 998244353, or taking each score modulo 998244353 and then summing?
Are we allowed to have S_i that are not integers? The prompt says positive integers, so that's clear.
When computing f(S_i/S_{i+1}), must we reduce S_i/S_{i+1} to lowest terms even if S_i and S_{i+1} are not coprime? Yes, by definition of f.
If S_i and S_{i+1} share a common factor, does that affect the condition f(S_i/S_{i+1}) = A_i? Since f reduces to lowest terms, it depends only on the reduced fraction, not the original values.
Is the gcd condition applied to the entire sequence S after constructing it, or must each pair S_i, S_{i+1} also be coprime? The condition only states gcd of all S_i equals 1.
Can S_i be arbitrarily large, or are they bounded? No explicit bound, but they must be positive integers satisfying the conditions.

Are we summing over all possible good sequences (including infinitely many if they exist), or is it guaranteed that there are finitely many? The problem likely expects finitely many, but not explicitly stated.
Does the order of the sequence matter? That is, are S_1,...,S_N considered as an ordered N-tuple, so permutations of the same multiset count separately if they satisfy conditions?
